changes: Add a sentence that after the transformation, a least-squares line is fitted to the transformed values, so the regression equation uses the transformed variable.
Note that the transformed variable is used as the explanatory variable in the Units 3 and 4 linear regression work.
match.reason: The bank card teaches the same transformations for straightening data, but it stops before fitting a line, which the Units 3 and 4 regression work needs.

confirm.reason: The bank point only transforms x, while VCE General Mathematics Units 3 and 4 expects students to choose squared, log or reciprocal transformations of either x or y (the circle of transformations) before fitting a line, so this course needs a broader, deeper point.

draft.title: Data transformations
card: A straight line fits poorly when a scatterplot is curved. A transformation changes one variable so the plot becomes closer to a straight line.
Three common transformations are squaring x (x²), taking the logarithm of x or y (log x), and taking the reciprocal of x (1/x).
Choose the transformation by the shape of the curve. After transforming, plot the new variable against the other one and check that the plot looks straighter.
Then fit the least squares line to the transformed data. Example: if y rises more and more steeply as x increases, try y against x², which can straighten the plot.
draft.remember: Transform a variable to straighten a curve, then fit a line to the straighter plot.

a.q: Why would a student transform x before fitting a line to a curved scatterplot?
opts: To make the relationship closer to a straight line
To make every data point sit exactly on the line
To change the response variable into the explanatory one
To remove the data points that are far from the others
a.why: A transformation reshapes the scale of a variable so a curved plot becomes closer to linear. It does not guarantee that points lie exactly on a line, and it does not remove any points.
a.clue: Think about what shape a line fits well.

b.q: Ava's scatterplot of y against x curves upward, getting steeper. She plots y against x² and the points now look roughly straight. What should she do next?
opts: Fit a least squares line to y against x²
Fit a least squares line to the original y against x
Delete the points that look furthest from the line
Swap the variables and plot x² against y
b.why: The straighter plot is y against x², so the line should be fitted to those transformed data. Fitting to the original data would use the curved plot, which a line fits poorly.
b.clue: Fit the line to the plot that looks straight.

a.best: To make the relationship closer to a straight line

b.best: Fit a least squares line to y against x²
